- Texas Tech K-12 does not operate on a traditional semester basis; courses are asynchronous.
- **Open Enrollment:** You can enroll in any course at any time and work at your own pace.
- **Tuition-Free Full-Time Program:** Enrollment is limited and uses a lottery system. Lottery windows are typically in the fall for the new school year and in January for mid-year transfers. If not selected, you’ll be placed on a waitlist and notified if a spot opens.
    - For the 2026-2027 school year:

- **Step 3:** Submit required documents (e.g., birth certificate, proof of residency, transcripts).
- **Step 4:** For tuition-free programs, if applying during a lottery window, your application will be placed in the lottery or on the waitlist.
- **Step 5:** Once accepted, you will receive login information and can begin course selection and enrollment.

**Important Notes**

- If you are enrolled in another district and want to take a single course, obtain approval from your school counselor before enrolling to ensure credit upon completion.
- Tuition-paid programs allow enrollment at any time, as long as space is available.
- For more details on program requirements and deadlines, see the [Academic Calendar](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/resources/academic-calendar/2026-2027/).

chunks.text:
What is a passing course grade?

Step 1: A passing course grade is 70% or higher.

Students must attempt all assignments in the course. The final exam will not be available until all assignments have been accepted and graded by the teacher.

Step 1: Students first attempt at the final exam will be Final Exam A.

Step 2: Students who score below 70% for the final exam will be eligible to retake the final exam one time.

Final Grade Point Calculation for Graduation

Texas Tech K-12 calculates a student’s final GPA using eligible coursework that applies toward high school graduation.

All accredited Texas Tech K-12 courses that apply toward graduation are included in the GPA calculation, except approved physical education substitution credits and local-credit courses. Grades transferred from accredited schools are also included in the final GPA unless the course is designated as local credit or graded on a pass/fail basis.

Texas Tech K-12 uses the following grade-point scale:

Grade to Points Conversion | Grade to Points Conversion | Grade to Points Conversion | Grade to Points Conversion

------------------------------------------------------------

Numerical Grade | Alphabetic Grade | Points for Regular Courses | Points for Honors, Advanced Placement, and Dual-Credit Courses

90-100 | A | 4.0 | 5.0

80-89 | B | 3.0 | 4.0

75-79 | C | 2.0 | 3.0

70-74 | D | 1.0 | 2.0

0-69 | F | 0.0 | 0.0

A failing grade earned in a Texas Tech K-12 course or Credit by Examination (CBE) may be replaced by successfully repeating the applicable course or examination in accordance with Texas Tech K-12 requirements.

answer.text:
**Course Transfer and Repetition Policy**

- **Transferring from an Accredited Public or Private School:**
  - Students will be placed in the appropriate grade level and semester courses based on the most recently completed semester as indicated on the student’s report card or other academic records from the previous school.
  - You will not have to repeat courses you have already passed and for which you can provide official documentation.

- **Transferring Before Completing a Semester:**
  - If you transfer before finishing a semester, you may be assigned intervention coursework, required to repeat the previous semester, or asked to complete placement assessments to determine the correct grade-level and course placement.

- **Transferring from Homeschool or Non-Accredited Programs:**
  - You must provide available academic documentation (transcripts, grade reports, or records of completed coursework).
  - Texas Tech K-12 will review your academic history and may require placement assessments or Credit by Exams (CBEs) to determine appropriate grade-level and course placement.

- **High School Credit Transfer:**
  - Accredited school transcripts are required upon enrollment and will be reviewed for awarding of credit.
  - Grades from accredited schools are included in your GPA unless the course is designated as local credit or graded on a pass/fail basis.
  - Homeschool or non-accredited program grades are not directly transferable for credit; you may need to complete the appropriate CBE or enroll in the corresponding course.

**Summary:**  
If you provide official transcripts from an accredited school showing you have passed certain courses, you will not have to repeat those courses. If you are coming from a homeschool or non-accredited program, you may need to take placement assessments or CBEs to establish credit.

**Next Steps:**  
- Prepare and submit your official transcripts or academic records during the enrollment process.
- If you have questions about your specific situation, contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.

What is Proctorio?

Our remote proctoring solution, Proctorio (opens in new tab), allows students to take an online exam anytime, anywhere, once they are ready, on their own schedule. There is no need to secure a proctor, arrange an exam time, and travel to the agreed-upon testing location. Students can take the exam from their home computer at any time.

Link for "Proctorio (opens in new tab)": https://proctorio.com/

Where do we take the tests?

The testing department will register you at an approved testing site closest to your home address. We understand that traveling long distances for these exams is not everyone’s first choice, If the site where you have been registered will not work for you, you may reach out to a local school and ask them to host your test. We will need confirmation from the local school, no later than 30 days before the 1st date of the testing window. Please also notify our testing department so that we are aware.

If you live outside of Texas, you will need to find an approved proctor to administer your tests. Reach out to your testing coordinator for more information on how to set up an approved testing proctor.

query.raw: Will I receive the same type of diploma as other Texas high school graduates?

chunks.text:
Graduation Requirements for Texas Tech High School Students

As a student enrolled in Texas Tech High School, you have several options for earning a high school diploma, depending on the date of your enrollment in ninth grade:

Step 1: Students enrolled in ninth grade before the 2014-15 school year must complete the Recommended High School Program (RHSP) or the Minimum High School Program (MHSP) and meet state testing requirements for your graduation plan. In some cases, you may be permitted to graduate on the Foundation Graduation Plan or the Foundation with Endorsement Graduation Plan and earn a Distinguished Level of Achievement.

Step 2: Students enrolled in ninth grade during or after the 2014-15 school year must complete the Foundation Graduation Plan plus Endorsement.

Step 3: For complete information regarding Texas graduation requirements, refer to the graduation section of the Texas Education Agency website (opens in new tab)

Link for "graduation section of the Texas Education Agency website (opens in new tab)": https://tea.texas.gov/academics/graduation-information/state-graduation-requirements

A Texas High School Diploma, From Anywhere in the World

The Single Diploma pathway is designed for students who want to complete their high school education through Texas Tech K-12.

Students complete Texas Tech K-12 curriculum entirely through online coursework and work toward earning a Texas high school diploma.

This pathway may be a good fit for students who:

Step 1: Want a fully online high school experience

Step 2: Want to earn a Texas high school diploma

Step 3: Need flexibility for when and where they learn

Step 4: Have strong English language skills

Step 5: Are prepared for rigorous reading, writing and communication in English

Because coursework is completed in English, strong English proficiency is important for student success.

Texas Tech High School Program Requirements

Texas Tech High School: As a full-time Texas Tech K-12 high school student, you must maintain academic progress in a minimum of four courses concurrently. Note: you will need to take more than the minimum number of courses to stay on grade level and graduate at your desired time.

To complete and retain admission as a student in Texas Tech High School, you must work with an academic advisor and be enrolled in a minimum of four Texas Tech K-12 courses (dual-credit and Credit By Exam's excluded). Generally, you will complete a total of six to seven credits per year (12-14 courses) and must also pass five State of Texas Assessment and Academic Readiness (STAAR) EOC (End of Course) exams to meet graduation requirements.

To graduate with a Texas Tech High School diploma, you will take at least your last year of high school credits (25%) from Texas Tech K-12. Exceptions will be considered by administration on a case-by-case basis but the last semester (2.5 credits) must be taken from Texas Tech K-12.

In addition to working towards a high school diploma, you may request a Verification Of Enrollment and Student ID (opens in new tab) cards. You may also participate in PSAT, ACT, AND SAT exams.

Link for "Student ID (opens in new tab)": https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/resources/documents/IdentityVerification.pdf

A Texas High School Diploma From Anywhere in the World

The Single Diploma pathway is designed for students who want to complete their high school education through Texas Tech K-12.

Students complete Texas Tech K-12 curriculum entirely through online coursework and work toward earning a Texas high school diploma.

This pathway may be a good fit for students who:

Step 1: Want a fully online high school experience

Step 2: Want to earn a Texas high school diploma

Step 3: Need flexibility for when and where they learn

Step 4: Have strong English language skills

Step 5: Are prepared for rigorous reading, writing and communication in English

Because coursework is completed in English, strong English proficiency is important for student success.

Weighted Coursework

Eligible Advanced Placement (AP), Honors, International Baccalaureate (IB) and Dual Credit/Concurrent Credit courses receive additional GPA weight in accordance with Texas Tech K-12 policy.

Eligible transferred coursework with an approved weighted-course designation may also receive the corresponding GPA weight when applied toward Texas Tech High School graduation requirements.

Transfer Grades for the High School Program

Students transferring to Texas Tech High School from an accredited public or private school must provide an official transcript, report card or other required academic records for evaluation.

Texas Tech K-12 will review eligible coursework to determine which credits may be applied toward the student’s Texas Tech High School graduation requirements. Transfer grades from accredited schools are included in the student’s GPA unless the course is designated as local credit or graded on a pass/fail basis.

Students transferring from a homeschool program or non-accredited school or program must provide appropriate academic documentation, such as transcripts or grade reports, for review. Grades from homeschool or non-accredited programs are not directly transferable for credit. Students may earn applicable credit by completing the appropriate CBE or by enrolling in the corresponding course.

Texas Tech K-12 reserves the right to make the final determination regarding the acceptance and application of transferred coursework toward Texas Tech High School graduation requirements.

The following designations will receive weighted credits:

Step 1: Advanced Placement (AP) or Passing (P)

Step 2: Honors

Step 3: International Baccalaureate (IB)

Step 4: Dual Credit/Concurrent Credit

All accredited Texas Tech K-12 courses taken by a student that apply to graduation will be used to compute the Grade Point Average, excluding any approved Physical Education Substitution (SUBPRO) credits and local credit courses.

Texas Tech K-12 academic advisors will make every effort to assist students in transferring grades and credits from accredited public or private schools as allowed by Texas Education Agency (TEA) policies and Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills (TEKS). An official transcript or report card will be required for credit transfer.

**SAT Testing for Texas Tech K-12 Students**

- Texas Tech K-12 does not directly administer the SAT exam.
- Students classified as juniors in Texas Tech High School should prepare to take the SAT and/or ACT.
- To participate, students must register for the SAT through the College Board website: [College Board (opens in new tab)](https://www.collegeboard.org/).
- When registering, use the Texas Tech University High School code: **444357**.

**Additional Information:**
- Contact the Texas Tech K-12 testing coordinator at ttuk12@ttu.edu for more information or assistance with SAT registration.
- SAT and ACT scores sent to Texas Tech University are not automatically sent to Texas Tech K-12. Notify your Texas Tech K-12 academic advisor and testing coordinator if you want your scores sent to the Texas Tech K-12 registrar’s office.

**Next Step:**
- Register for the SAT on the College Board website and use the school code 444357.

If you need further assistance, contact the Texas Tech K-12 testing coordinator at ttuk12@ttu.edu or call 1-800-692-6877.
